Carlos —

Appreciate the clear list. To keep this tight for your audit team, we've drafted a one-page Egress Accountability Charter that captures exactly what you asked for and the evidence bundle you can expect from us during onboarding. High-level items covered:

1) Owner: Redwood Network Operations (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — point of contact for IP custody and rotation notifications.
2) Exit channels: distinct control-plane and runtime/data egress paths listed with recommended NAT mode (customer NAT or Redwood-managed NAT).
3) Static vs ephemeral: recommended static / reserved IP blocks for production; ephemeral rotation plan for non-prod.
4) Evidence package: list of egress IPs (CIDRs), sample packet captures/traceroutes to destination FQDNs, signed acknowledgement of ownership, and DNS/SNI behavior notes.
5) Exception process: temporary exceptions with expiry and audit trail.
6) Ops runbook: handoff to your NetOps with test checklist (connectivity tests, SNI validation, TLS fingerprint).

Questions for you:
- Will Valencia accept Redwood-provided static IPs, or do you require customer-run NAT in front of the private endpoint?
- Could you return a list of expected external destinations (SaaS vendor FQDNs) so we can map which addresses must be reachable?

I've attached the charter (redwood-egress-accountability-charter-v1.pdf) as a starting point. If you confirm the NAT model and provide expected destinations, we'll produce the assertion packet (signed PDF + CSV of IPs) within 48 business hours.

If it helps, Marissa can coordinate the DocuSign for the ownership acknowledgment and Laura can help align the acceptance tests.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
